meta.name: Classify cold email replies and route leads with Gmail, Gemini, Slack and Sheets

name: Cold Email Reply Classifier and Auto-Router-n8nSubmission

parameters.content:
## Cold Email Reply Classifier & Auto-Router

Most sales teams lose hot replies because they're buried under auto-replies, objections, and "not interested" messages. By the time someone spots a genuine lead, the prospect has already moved on.

This workflow fixes that. It watches your outreach inbox, reads every reply using AI, and instantly alerts your team but only when action is needed.

Every reply gets classified into one of five categories:

- **Interested** — prospect wants to learn more or book a call
- **Question** — prospect is asking something specific
- **Objection** — pushback, but the conversation is still live
- **Not Interested** — clear decline
- **Auto-Reply** — out-of-office or automated bounce

Actionable replies trigger a Slack alert and an AI-written draft saved to Gmail Drafts. Your rep reviews and sends manually — the AI never sends on your behalf. Every reply is logged to Google Sheets regardless of outcome.

---

### Requirements

- Gmail OAuth2
- Google Gemini API Key
- Google Sheets OAuth2
- Slack OAuth2 (Bot Token)

---

### Setup

1. Create a Gmail label called **Outreach-Replies**
2. Create a Gmail filter that applies this label to inbound replies only
3. Add **-from:me** to the filter to exclude your own sent emails
4. Invite your Slack bot to **#outreach-replies** using `/invite @YourBotName`
5. Create a Google Sheet with headers matching the column mapping in the storage node
6. Activate the workflow — it polls Gmail every minute

---

### Customization

- **Add or remove categories** — edit the prompt in the AI node and update the routing condition to match
- **Alert on Objections** — add Objection as a second condition on the routing node
- **Change poll frequency** — adjust the trigger interval for high-volume inboxes
- **Widen the filter** — update the Gmail filter criteria to cover additional campaigns or aliases

## Gmail Label Polling Trigger

Polls Gmail every minute for new emails carrying the **Outreach-Replies** label. A Gmail label and filter must be created manually before executing — see the warning note beside this node.

## Full Reply Body Extraction

Fetches the complete reply by thread ID and strips the quoted original email before passing text to the AI.
Stripping quoted content is critical — without it, the AI reads your own outreach pitch as part of the reply and misclassifies it.

## Gemini Reply Classification

Gemini reads the cleaned reply and returns a category, confidence score, reasoning, and a suggested reply draft in a single call.
If the response fails to parse, the reply is flagged **Needs Manual Review** rather than dropped — check the execution log for that run.

## Slack Alert and Draft Reply

Interested and Question replies trigger a Gmail draft and a Slack alert with a direct link to that draft.
All other replies are logged only — this is intentional, not a missing step. The workflow never sends email automatically.

## Google Sheets Reply Tracker

Every reply is logged here before any routing decision — nothing is lost even if no action is taken.
A row showing **Needs Manual Review** means the AI response failed to parse — classify that reply manually.

## Gmail Label and Filter Required

Create a Gmail label called **Outreach-Replies** and a filter that applies it to inbound replies.
Always add **-from:me** to the filter — without it, your own outbound emails get picked up and misclassified as prospect replies.

## Slack Bot Channel Access

Create a channel named **#outreach-replies**. Invite your Slack bot to **#outreach-replies** before activating: `/invite @YourBotName`
Without this, Slack alerts will fail silently with no error shown in the execution log.
